rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 10 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7941, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'PARTY-LIST SYSTEM ACT'
rows.abstract: Rationale: Under the provisions of said R.A. No. 7941 particularly Section 10 thereof which gives the voter a second vote naming the party, organization, or coalition he wants represented in the House of Representatives in effect making the varioussectors fight each other to get a seat in congress, there is a distinct probability that certain sectors may not succeed in putting their representatives in Congress, thus defeating the very purpose of the Constitution in mandating a party-list election. >Amends, therefore, Section 10 of RA 7941 to read as follows: "Section 10. - Manner of Voting. Every voter shall be entitled to ONE VOTE [two (2) votes: the first is a vote] for candidate for member of the House of Representatives in his legislaative district, and ONE VOTE EACH FOR A PARTY AND THE TWELVE (12) SECTORAL ORGANIZATIONS ENUMERATED IN SECTION 5 OF THIS ACT, THE RESPECTIVE VOTE TO BE CAST FOR THE PARTY, ORGANIZATION OR COALITION REPRESENTING A PARTICULAR SECTOR CHOSEN BY THE VOTER
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 1996-11-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION EIGHTY-NINE OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED ONE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND FORTY-FIVE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE GOVERNMENT AUDITING CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING PENALTY THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES(RE: CASH ADVANCES)
rows.abstract: "SECTION 89 of the government Auditing Code was designed to control the giving of cash advance to any official or employee, but the existing provision of the law is not effective because it DOES NOT PROVIDE A PENALTY for those who intend to vioaltethe said provision, hence the rampant violation of its and the lrage accumulation of unliquidated cash advances in the different department, bureaus and offices." "CASH ADVANCE SHALL INCLUDE (1) CASH ADVANCE TO DULY DESIGNATED SPECCIAL DISBURSING OFFICERS FOR SPECIFIC AUTHORIZED OFFICIAL EXPENDITURES AND (2) CASH ADVANCE TO OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE VARIOUS AGENCIES OF THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AND ALL LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS FOR AUTHORIZED DISBURSEMENTS." > Penalizes any official or employee oof the national government and the local government units who violates this provision with a PRINCIPAL PENALTY OF PRISION CORRECTIONAL AND AN ACCESSORY PENALTY OF PERPETUAL DISQUALIFICATIO N FROM PUBLIC OFFICE.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION OF THE SCHOOL HEALTH AND NUTRITION PROGRAM (SHNP) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, CULTURE AND SPORTS, AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "School Health and Nutrition Act" Rationale: "Health consciousness and proper health care should be inculcated in the minds of even the young.  From a tender age of six years old, a child is required to attend school for at least five to six hours,five days a week, for eight months in a year. Unfortunately, not much emphasis is given to school health and nutrition program. It must be recognized tht it is the status of children's health and nutrition tht determines their capacity for learning.Aims to upgrade the SHNP of the DECS to enhance the active learning capacity of the chidlren, and for the teachers and other non-teaching personnel to function most effectively and efficiently this, enabling the achievement of the goals of quality baasic education. Provides for the principal thrusts, objectives, components and priority programs of the SHNP modernization.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 1996-11-11

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROTECTING PRIVACY OF INFORMATION WITHIN THE PRIVATE SECTOR
rows.abstract: "Private Sector Privacy Act" Rationale: The 20th Century is characterized by advances in information technology which has revolutionalize d all areas of human endeavor, particularly in business and marketing. All transactions among companies ares tored in databases that practicallt reveal all vital information regarding an individual's personel and financial status. Thus, access to such information as address, age, can be easily obtained without due permission from the actual person. This is aclear violation of privacy and the protection of the individual against any damage arising from such unauthorized revelation and dissemination. Provides for these significant concerns: (1) instances when the disclosure of processing of personal datashall be considered; (2) circumstances that should be present ti oresume that a data subject shall be deemed to have given his or her consent; (3) rights of data subjects; and (4) responsibilitie s of Private Sector Personal Data Processor (PDPs).

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENCOURAGE SAVINGS MOBILIZATION BY GRANTING TAX PRIVILEGES TO SMALL DEPOSITORS
rows.abstract: Rationale: The importance of savings as a catalyst of economic growth cannot be underscored. It is savings, after all, which generates the broad base of investible funds which, in turn, are responsible for business formation, industrial build-up, employment and income creation, among others. Entitles, therefore, tax privileges to small depositors by allowing them to use the twenty per cent (20%) final withholding tax paid on their interest income as tax credit or tax refund pursuant to terms and conditions specified in this Act. Defines SMALL DEPOSITORS to refer to any individual with an aggregate annual savings account not exceeding five hudnred thousand pesos (P500,000.00) per year.

rows.author: B009
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR RECOGNITION AND PROTECTION OF PRIOR AND VESTED ANCESTRAL LAND AND MINING RIGHTS OF INDIGENOUS CULTURAL COMMUNITIES OR MEMBERS THEREOF WITHIN PATENTED MINING CLAIMS AND MINING LEASES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Intends to rectify the injustice inflicted by the Philippine Bill of 1902 insidiously used by the Americans to take over ancestral mines of indigenous natives by restoring their rights over whatever remains of their ancestral lands and mines. Proposes that patented mining claims over which mining operations have ceased shall revert back to the State. Bans the "OPEN PIT" mining method where it is destructive to human settlements, small-scale mining and to the environment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 1996-11-12

rows.author: A006
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING A FOREIGN EXCHANGE POLICY FAVORABLE TO THE PROMOTION OF PHILIPPINE EXPORTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7653, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CENTRAL BANK ACT
rows.abstract: Aims to improve the competitiveness of Philippine enterprises, especially the exporters, and to reduce considerably the risk of exporting attributable to foreign exchange fluctuations. Amends, therefore, certain provisions of Republic Act No. 7653 with these proposals, in order to provide a policy for the pursuance of a competitive exchange rate: (1) Adding in the mandate of the BSP the objective of a competitive exchange rate; (2) Requiring the BSP to report once a year to Congress on how thepolicy pursued has supported the economic development programs and thrusts of the government; (3) Providing for exporters' representation the Monetary Board; and (4) Creating a consultation mechanism through which the competitive rate of foreign exchhange is determined or set.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 1996-11-12

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INCENTIVES FOR COMPANIES WITHIN SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONES TO JOINTLY ESTABLISH COOPERATIVE GENERAL HOSPITALS OR INDUSTRIAL CLINICS FOR THE HEALTH AND SAFETY OF WORKERS AND THEIR FAMILIES WITHIN SUCH ZONES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Ecozone Hospitals Incentives Act of 1996" Mandates that all employers located in a declared special economic zone shall, in cooperation with workers organizations and government agencies, establish an emergency general hospital or industrial clinicwhich shall render exclusive medical, dental and occupational health and safety services for workers and their families, as well as all resident within the economic zone. Provides incentives and tax exemption privileges to such companies who shall cooperate in the establishment of said cooperative general hospital.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1996-11-12

rows.author: B038
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING PRIVATE LANDOWNERS FROM PAYMENT OF REAL PROPERTY TAXES WHOSE LANDS ARE OCCUPIED BY SQUATTERS
rows.abstract: Rationale: The squatter problem has become a national menace that even with the existence of a law making the act of squatting punishable under P.D. 772, the government seems  to be losing the war on squatting. In fact, the war is raging with all those numerous demolition activities being udnertaken presently by the local govenrment units. Grants, therefore, TAX RELIEF to those hapless landowners who are being deprived of the use of their properties, until such time that the government can clear their lands from squatters.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 1996-11-12
